findings.where: Nav bar (the gummed binding) at both widths: the aqueduct mark and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark beside it
findings.fault: The logo appears only recoloured. The three arches are drawn pale canary on the binding red, not in the logo grey #404040, and 'MMM INFRA' is set in pale yellow Caslon capitals, not the logo's blue Georgia. Mark holds no reversed or one-colour version of his logo, so this is a version made without his yes. Nowhere on the tile can he see his actual logo sitting on the pad.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo is the one fixed brand element the site must keep and build in the opening animation (brief, value 7). He would see his mark in colours he never chose and a wordmark in a different typeface, and could not tell from this tile whether his real logo works on a legal pad. The brief says the mark is never redrawn, and the house rule says a logo is never recoloured.

findings.where: Palette swatches (style tile, below the first screen, both widths)
findings.fault: The palette leaves out the logo's two colours, logo blue #0070C0 and logo grey #404040. It does not give them a job or mark them as logo-only. Its blues, Ballpoint #1B2A6B and Light hand #34407A, are navies picked without reference to the logo blue. So the tile does not show how the logo's colours sit beside the pad's ink and binding.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the layout round that draws inside this look. Mark has not opened his logo colours (brand sheet §2), so they stay fixed and the palette should be built around them. Without them, the next round must guess whether the ballpoint navy and the logo blue may share a view, or whether they read as a near-miss.

findings.where: Article specimen at desktop: the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' and its byline 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024'
findings.fault: The two lines of the title are set two feints (64 px) apart, so the gap between them is wider than the gap between the title and its own byline. The italic byline sits almost on the title's descenders. The hero heading is set tight at 64/64, and so is the same title on phone, so like headings are treated unalike. At desktop the title reads as two separate headings, and the byline reads as attached to the second.
findings.who_objects: A reader opening one of Mark's articles, the page's Read mode: the title does not hold together as one line of thought. Angélique, who will post many articles into this template, would also object, because the double-spaced heading is the treatment every long title will get.
